title: A new fish changes the river

scenes.tts: In the nineteen seventies and eighties, people put blue catfish into Virginia's rivers. Blue catfish come from the Mississippi River basin. Today they are common in parts of those rivers. So what happens to a river when people bring in a big new fish?

scenes.tts: People are part of ecosystems. We depend on them for food, water and energy. A habitat is the place where an organism finds food, water and shelter. A population is all members of one species in one area at one time. Land use is how people use land, like farms, homes or roads.
scenes.visual: people inside an ecosystem with food, water, energy; habitat; population; land use
scenes.narration: People are part of ecosystems. We depend on them for food, water and energy. A habitat is the place where an organism finds food, water and shelter. A population is all members of one species in one area at one time. Land use is how people use land, like farms, homes or roads.

scenes.tts: Taking resources, like wood or gravel, changes habitats too. Habitat destruction is damage that removes or ruins a habitat. Filling in a marsh to build homes is one example. Animals there must move or die, so their populations often drop. Pollution is harmful material added to air, water or soil. Extra fertilizer in a river can feed fast algae growth.

scenes.tts: A native species lives in a place naturally, without people bringing it. White catfish are native to Virginia's Bay rivers. An invasive species is brought to a new place, spreads and causes harm to native species or to people. Being new is not enough. It must spread and cause harm.
scenes.visual: native white catfish; blue catfish brought in; three-part test with checks
scenes.narration: A native species lives in a place naturally, without people bringing it. White catfish are native to Virginia's Bay rivers. An invasive species is brought to a new place, spreads and causes harm to native species or to people. Being new is not enough. It must spread and cause harm.

scenes.tts: Competition is when species need the same resource and there is not enough. It does not need a fight. Blue catfish eat fish and sometimes blue crabs. Scientists report white catfish eat similar prey. So the two may compete for food. If blue catfish eat many of these, less is left for white catfish.
scenes.visual: two catfish reach for one shared food supply; no fight; supply shrinks
scenes.narration: Competition is when species need the same resource and there is not enough. It does not need a fight. Blue catfish eat fish and sometimes blue crabs. scenes.tts: A food web links species by who eats whom. So a change in one population can spread through the whole web. Suppose blue catfish eat many blue crabs. Then fewer may be left for other crab eaters, including people. So what happens when people bring in a big new fish? Some populations go up, and others go down. The change spreads through the food web.
